content:
According to web traffic analysis data from 9to5Mac, Apple is testing iOS 27.0.1 for iPhone. The update is expected to focus on bug fixes and system performance improvements.

iOS 27.0.1 is coming soon

9to5Mac's analytics data began showing traces of iOS 27.0.1 a few days ago, and MacRumors has also reported on it.

Apple told 9to5Mac this morning that it will release a software update early next week to fix an issue causing some iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max devices to restart automatically after Face ID recognition fails.

We reported on this issue earlier this week, explaining that when you try to use Face ID to unlock apps like "Passwords," your iPhone may unexpectedly restart if Face ID recognition fails.

I personally have never been able to reproduce this issue on an iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max, but clearly a significant number of users are affected. The good news is this is a software-fixable bug, not a hardware fault.

iOS 27.0.1 will very likely (though not yet confirmed) address the aforementioned issue. The update may also include other bug fixes for iOS 27 and the new iPhone 18 Pro hardware.

Since upgrading to iOS 27, have you encountered any issues? What about iPhone 18 Pro-specific issues? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
